statement: Solve $\frac{dy}{dx}=y(1-y)$ with $y(0)=\frac12$. (i) Find $y$ explicitly. (ii) Find $\lim_{x\to\infty}y(x)$. (iii) Describe the behaviour as $x\to-\infty$.
solution: (i) Separate: $\frac{dy}{y(1-y)}=dx$. Since $\frac1{y(1-y)}=\frac1y+\frac1{1-y}$, integrating gives $\ln|y|-\ln|1-y|=x+C$, so $\frac{y}{1-y}=Ae^{x}$. With $y(0)=\frac12$: $A=1$. Hence $y=e^{x}(1-y)\Rightarrow y=\frac{e^{x}}{1+e^{x}}=\frac1{1+e^{-x}}$. (ii) As $x\to\infty$, $e^{-x}\to0$, so $y\to1$. (iii) As $x\to-\infty$, $e^{x}\to0$, so $y\to0$.
hints: Apply the initial condition to fix A.
